claims.text: Sequence-level probability estimates given by LLMs have limitations as reliable indicators of generation quality.
LLMs demonstrate strong calibration at the token level, particularly when choosing correct answers in multiple-choice questions or evaluating true/false statements.
Open-ended generation tasks can be reformulated into token-level prediction tasks to leverage LLMs' token-level calibration.
Self-evaluation based scores improve accuracy in selective generation.
Self-evaluation based scores correlate better with the overall quality of generated content than probability-based metrics.

evidence.description: Citing recent research demonstrating the limitations of likelihood-based metrics such as perplexity.
Experiments with PaLM-2 and GPT-3 on TruthfulQA and TL;DR benchmarks show accuracy improvements using self-evaluation scoring.
Experimental evaluation with PaLM-2 and GPT-3 demonstrates better correlation with content quality.

methodologies.name: Self-Evaluation via Token-Level Reformulation
methodologies.description: Instructing an LLM to self-evaluate generated answers using multi-way comparison or point-wise evaluation reformulated as token-level prediction tasks.

limitations.text: Sequence-level probability estimates given by LLMs are not reliable indicators of generation quality.
